_readme: How each creative dial is said to a picture model (PSH-10 (dials as picture words)). `picture` dials are sent as ONE concrete instruction for a still: the brand step's own line for this picture when it wrote one at that level, else the phrase below. `writing` dials act on how the ad was written; they stay on the sheet and reach the picture through the swaps and the words, never as a line. `film` dials do not exist in a still. The dial's level wording in components/creative-controls/controls.json is never sent verbatim (a dictionary definition is drawn literally).
history: 2026-10-26: created after the dial definitions were found reaching the picture prompt word for word. 2026-10-29: `built_in` and `set` added for the 3D-set chain; light, size, distance and density are built, not said; the new dressing dial (the concept and the moment) added; density 0 no longer asks for a plain background.
_set_readme: Since 2026-10-28 every picture is a 3D set at true sizes, printed into a photo, the words set on top (tools/image-production CLAUDE.md, 'Every picture: a 3D set, printed, then the words'). `built_in` says where each picture dial is made: `set` = built in the 3D set (sizes, distance, how much is in frame, where the light comes from and how hard, what the surfaces and props are made of), never said to the print; `print` = said to the print step (materials, grain, skin, how real it looks); `cast` = the person's own reference and face direction. `set` gives, per level, what to build. `levels` stay the words for a picture made without a set.

levels.0: Faces relaxed and still; soft, even light.
levels.1: A calm face, a small reaction; ordinary light.
levels.2: An alert face, something at stake; clear light.
levels.3: A strong reaction on the face: tight jaw, wide eyes; hard light.
levels.4: The strongest reaction the face can hold, caught at its peak; hard, direct light.

set.0: Soft, broad light from one side; nothing in the set at an angle.
set.1: One soft key light, ordinary room light.
set.2: A clear key light, a firmer shadow edge.
set.3: A hard key light at a low angle; long, sharp shadows across the surface.
set.4: One hard, direct light close to the subject; deep, sharp shadows, the peak moment posed.

levels.-2: The problem shown at its worst, full size, in unflattering hard light.
levels.-1: The problem visible and uncomfortable, nothing softened.
levels.1: Warm light, an easy, relieved face.
levels.2: Bright light, a delighted face, the result plainly visible.

set.-2: Hard, cold, top-down light on the problem; the problem prop at full size, nearest the camera.
set.-1: Cool, plain light; the problem visible, nothing hiding it.
set.2: Bright, warm light with a soft fill; the result in the sharpest plane.

levels.0: An obviously illustrated or rendered picture.
levels.1: A clean studio photo, idealised but believable.
levels.2: A natural-light photo in a real place, lightly edited.
levels.3: Phone-camera photo: real skin texture with pores, slight noise, imperfect framing, nothing retouched.
levels.4: A raw documentary snapshot: unposed, unretouched, real place and moment.

levels.2: Visible compression, like a reposted screenshot.
levels.3: A heavy phone filter over the whole picture.
levels.4: Blown-out colour, crushed blacks and heavy noise.

levels.0: One subject alone on one real surface, nothing else in the frame.
levels.1: The subject and only a hint of the place around it.
levels.2: A full scene with a few supporting things.
levels.3: A busy scene with many things in it.
levels.4: Packed edge to edge with things.

set.0: One subject on the scene's one surface; no other prop in the set.
set.1: The subject and one or two props at the frame's edge.
set.2: A full set: the subject plus a few supporting props at true size.
set.3: Many props, overlapping, all at true size.
set.4: Props edge to edge, stacked and filling every surface.

levels.1: One thing a little bigger than it should be.
levels.2: One thing clearly too big for the scene.
levels.3: One thing enormous against the person, the rest true size.
levels.4: One thing impossibly huge or impossibly tiny.

set.0: Every object at its true size.
set.1: One prop modelled a little bigger than true size.
set.2: One prop modelled clearly too big for the set.
set.3: One prop modelled at monumental size against the rest; the product stays its true size.
set.4: One prop modelled impossibly huge or tiny; the product stays its true size unless it is the joke, shown once.

levels.0: Nothing about the scene feels off.
levels.1: One small detail is slightly too neat or too regular.
levels.2: The place feels empty and in-between.
levels.3: Almost real, with something quietly unsettling.
levels.4: Disturbing but impossible to look away from.

set.1: One object placed a little too neatly, squared to the camera.
set.2: An empty set with too much floor or wall; flat, fluorescent light.
set.3: A camera angle slightly too low or too high; one light from an odd place.
set.4: A direct on-camera flash, hard shadow behind everything; one object where it cannot be.

levels.0: Extreme wide: the person small in a big place.
levels.1: Wide: the whole body and the place.
levels.3: Close-up: the face or the hand fills the frame.
levels.4: Extreme close-up: skin and pores fill the frame.

set.0: The set camera far back on a wide lens; the subject small.
set.1: Camera back far enough for the whole subject and the set.
set.2: Camera at mid distance, subject from the waist or the middle up.
set.3: Camera close on a normal phone lens; the subject fills the frame.
set.4: Camera at the closest focus; one detail fills the frame.

levels.0: The person has no idea a camera is there.
levels.1: A passing glance, not at the camera.
levels.2: Caught in profile in the moment, eyes off the camera.
levels.4: Looking into the camera and gesturing at the viewer.

levels.1: No logos and no recognisable faces anywhere.
levels.2: Any logo or famous look is changed slightly: one letter off, the shape bent.
levels.3: Any logo or famous mark is renamed into an obvious joke about the problem.
levels.4: Any logo or famous mark is rebuilt out of the problem itself.

set.1: Props carry no logos or marks.
set.2: Each prop's mark is modelled one letter off or bent.
set.3: Each prop's mark is renamed into a joke about the problem, printed on the prop.
set.4: Each prop's mark is built from the problem itself.

levels.0: Ordinary people with no cultural reference.
levels.1: Ordinary people; the reference is only in the words.
levels.2: A known look or setting in the background.
levels.3: The lead is a lookalike of a known figure, clearly not the real person.
levels.4: The whole picture is built around a known figure's lookalike, clearly not the real person.

set.1: No reference props; the reference is in the words.
set.2: One prop or surface from the reference's world, in the background.
set.3: The set dressed around the lookalike lead: the props and surfaces of that person's known world.
set.4: The whole set is the known moment's world.

levels.0: The swipe's own surfaces, props and colours.
levels.1: The prop that marks the swipe's moment becomes the same prop for our moment, same size and place.
levels.2: The moment's colours on every surface, and the moment's prop in its place.
levels.3: Every surface and prop made from the concept's world, the moment's name printed on one real prop.
levels.4: The whole frame is the concept's world, down to every texture.

set.0: Build the swipe's own surfaces and props as they are.
set.1: Replace the swipe's moment prop with ours, same model size and place; its sign carries the moment's name.
set.2: The moment's palette as the materials on every surface; the moment prop in place.
set.3: Swap every surface material and prop for the concept's version at true size; the moment's name as lettering on one real prop.
set.4: Every surface, prop and texture from the concept's world; the swipe's layout and camera untouched.

writing_reason: not applicable to the picture prompt: acts on the writing, already carried by the swaps and the words
film_reason: not used in a still picture
